model_annotation: Figure 4 illustrates how knowledge-probing performance (ACC) varies with the “Co-occurrence Number” for several editing methods and a non-edited baseline. The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” shown on a logarithmic scale with major ticks at approximately \(10^1\), \(10^2\), and \(10^3\), spanning from values below \(10^1\) (leftmost points) to above \(10^3\) (rightmost points). The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)” on a linear scale, ranging from 40 to 65 with ticks every 5 units. Six lines are plotted: Base is a black solid line with circular markers that rises from about 40 at the leftmost x-value to about 44 at the rightmost x-value; FT is a blue solid line with triangular markers increasing from about 43 to about 48; IKE is a red solid line with x-shaped markers increasing from about 44 to about 49; MEND is a brown solid line with plus-shaped markers increasing from about 44 to about 55; MEMIT is a purple solid line with star markers rising from about 44 to about 53–54; ROME is a green solid line with square markers starting near 50 and increasing to about 66 at the highest co-occurrence number, with intermediate points near the mid-50s around \(10^1\) and low-60s around \(10^2\).
